newsitem.title: USA: U.S. domestic crudes weaken on trade selling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. domestic crudes weaken on trade selling.

text.p: U.S. crudes edged slightly lower late Friday on some refiners selling heavily and upon Iraq stating it would not attack U.S. air patrols of "no-fly zones" in northern and southern Iraq.
Oct West Texas Intermediate/Cushing fell about 60 cents to $24.45-55 a barrel from Thursday, with the Iraq gesture seen reducing tensions.
But despite the day's losses, traders said the market's uptrend was intact, supported by low stocks and refinery runs.
One refiner who sold some light grades lower today could be in possession of new foreign supplies, traders said.
Domestic grades had also been pressured all session by the rise in outright prices, which reached a high of $25.35.

The refiner was seen a big seller of Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire, easing from a premium of 16 cents against WTI to parity, before recovering to plus 2/3 cents. The grade was at a 20-cent premium on Thursday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James also dropped from plus 30 cents to 22 cts against WTI, down as much as 12 cents.
Midland/WTI was sold at 3-4 cents over WTI, down several notches from Thursday, with WTI/Cushing Posting Plus easing to $2.33/37 a barrel, down from trades at $2.43-45.
The rumored sale of one million barrels of Brent into the U.S. Gulf today intensified pressure on sweets, traders said.
Heavy, sours were challenged by supplies of Cano Limon and Oriente crudes, but differentials were only a shade weaker.
Eugene Island traded at WTI minus $1.10, down four cents, and West Texas Sour moved at minus $1.20, down the same.
